about: Copper-temperature basis registry for gates/cu_temp_basis.py. One entry per consumer of copper resistance or copper loss in the scorecard input chain that does not carry its own explicit temperature. basis_temp_c is the copper temperature the code assumes; direction is the side that is conservative for THAT consumer's verdict; a 'hot is conservative' consumer must sit at or above hot_floor_c, a 'cold is conservative' one at or below cold_ceil_c, or carry an unexpired waiver. Audit: tmp/cu-temp-audit/README.md (2026-10-15).

scan.not_scanned_note: Older rounds (round1-4, native-0x..1x power-probes) and candidate studies under 11-candidates are outside the scorecard input chain; the audit README lists them.

consumers.consumer: B3 board-thermal model, ratings gate inputs and the R5 derating / via checks (hot copper, S17)
consumers.basis_how: copper loss q = q20 (1 + 0.00393 (T - 20)) at each cell's solved absolute temperature (fixed-J, conservative by Thomson's principle); r5_vias17 barrel rho(T) at the via mid-wall; run files record copper_temp_model and b3_ratings_gate refuses cold runs
consumers.justification: S17 closed by the B3 hot-copper lane (b3-ratings/hot-copper-2026-10-15/). --copper-tcr 0 reproduces the 20 C margins byte for byte (control).

consumers.consumer: Dated B3 studies (audit, line-hold, refine, heat attribution) kept as records at 20 C copper
consumers.justification: Historical study records dated before S17 closed; they feed no gate. Their 20 C basis is stated in their READMEs; current numbers come from CU-01.

consumers.consumer: Task 04 A4 producers and index (A4 loss fields, via_currents.json, summary.json)
consumers.basis_how: default (solver.Net(...) without temp_c); run_board.py:312 lists '20 C copper'
consumers.justification: The A4 fields are solved at 20 C as a reference; B3 (CU-01) applies the copper TCR at the solved temperature before any verdict.

consumers.consumer: R5 derating (r5-derating/r5_derating.py), pre-G6 script on B3 pad temperatures at 20 C
consumers.basis_how: inherited from B3 pad temperature; RHO_CU 1.72e-8 at 20 C (no TCR) in r5_vias17.py
consumers.justification: Superseded by G6 (stage17-r5/g6_r5_derating.py, in CU-01): R5 derating on the hot-copper B3 solve, 32.6 % on s45 (DECISIONS 61). This pre-G6 script (DECISIONS 14, WSK2512 era) is kept as the record of that verdict; G6's control A cites its committed results.json numbers, not this code.

consumers.consumer: Fuse-copper fusing ratio (fuse_copper_fusing_ratio): Onderdonk neck I2t at the pre-fault copper temperature; cord resistance for the let-through
consumers.basis_how: explicit: TA_HOT = 105 (neck fusing, hot); RHO_CU 1.724e-8 at 20 C for the cord/branch R (cold); 25 C also reported
consumers.justification: Fusing I2t falls with Ta (hot conservative); prospective current rises as source R falls (cold conservative). min_ratio_all is 0.993 at Ta 105; it crosses 1.0 at Ta ~102 C, so the sign hinges on the pre-fault neck temperature (estimate in the audit).

consumers.consumer: F2 coordination (cord/branch/panel copper loop for let-through current)
consumers.basis_how: explicit: RHO_CU20 'cold = max current'; Cu=0 variants evaluated as the stiffest bound
consumers.justification: Lower R = higher fault current, so cold copper and Cu=0 are the conservative side for let-through.

consumers.consumer: Kelvin plane solve (OCP threshold shift from the In1 Kelvin pour), kit Net with explicit temp_c
consumers.justification: A positive threshold error e_th lowers the trip; hot copper raises e_th. 125 C is above the 83-112 C tank copper but the Kelvin pour sits beside R5, whose pad reaches 135 C (c28/h25) to 162 C (c28/h10): first-order effect +2.8 % to +10 % on e_th (-0.06 to -0.21 A on the band low edge).

consumers.consumer: Kelvin budget (kelvin_band_low_A scorecard metric): reads plane-TAG.json from CU-08
consumers.basis_how: derived from kelvin_plane.py (125 C) for the low edge; the high edge takes zero shift
consumers.justification: Low edge: hot-copper census shift (down). High edge: unshifted (zero return current = cold bound). Both ends of the band are bounded, so a TCR miss cannot widen it past the stated bound.

consumers.consumer: Kelvin track-only bound (Rayleigh monotone bound; not in the chain, kept explicit)
consumers.basis_how: explicit: 1.72e-8 x (1 + 0.00393 x 100) is 120 C although the comment says 125 C
consumers.justification: Label mismatch only (1.5 % in rho, 1.4137 vs 1.393). Also uses 50 um copper (thinner than 70 um), so the bound stays conservative.

consumers.consumer: Tank-path neck fin estimate (stage 15, 22 / 28 A local copper rise; ESTIMATE, not a gate)
consumers.basis_how: explicit but mislabelled: RHO = 1.72e-8 x (1 + 0.00393 x 75) is 95 C, comment says 100 C
consumers.justification: Superseded by the hot-copper B3 solve (CU-01), which is the gate for local tank-copper temperature on the board of record (DECISIONS 61). The stage-15 estimate is kept as a record; its RHO is 95 C although the comment says 100 C, and at 130-160 C copper the estimate would read about 33.6-36.4 K instead of 30.4 K.

consumers.consumer: IPC-2221 20 K tank-width screen (sw_widths.py; sets the stage-15 9.77-9.82 mm tank-copper width)
consumers.basis_how: none stated: the IPC-2221 fit assumes copper near ambient (~25 C) + the 20 K rise = ~45 C
consumers.justification: Superseded by the hot-copper B3 solve (CU-01): the tank-copper width is now judged by the B3 laminate / part rows at solved copper temperature, not by the IPC-2221 20 K screen. Kept as the stage-15 record; on hot copper the screen would ask about 10.7 mm instead of 9.82 mm (estimate).

consumers.consumer: Kit sheet solver library (Net default temp_c = 20, RHO_CU, ALPHA_CU) and its closed-form self-test
consumers.basis_how: library default; every caller must pass temp_c or register
consumers.justification: Reference temperature of the constants; the self-test compares against closed forms at 20 C. Not a physical claim about any board.
Solver validation against analytic strips; resistance ratios, not a board claim.

consumers.consumer: Undated B3 diagnostics and convergence scripts still on 20 C copper (h10-stall, stage-15b snapshots, b3-convergence run / report)
consumers.basis_how: inherited 20 C or pre-S17 run files
consumers.justification: Diagnostics and convergence studies on 20 C copper, superseded by the hot-copper B3 solve (CU-01) for every current number (DECISIONS 61); kept as records. Re-run on hot copper before citing any of them again.

consumers.consumer: B3 hot-copper and airflow tests (cold runs are the controls)
consumers.justification: Tests compare the hot model against cold controls and closed forms; no board claim.
